belief: My spiritual gifts don’t matter as much as other people’s.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that your spiritual gifts don’t matter as much as other people’s, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A church culture that celebrated only up-front gifts like preaching, singing, or leading. Being overlooked or compared with a more talented sibling or friend. Quiet personality or behind-the-scenes service that rarely gets thanked. Low self-esteem that dismisses anything you do well. Thinking that a gift must be dramatic to be important.
teaches: Every believer receives gifts from the Spirit for the good of the whole body. God Himself placed each member where He wanted. Paul says the parts that seem weaker are actually indispensable. A kind word, a meal, a prayer, a faithful act of service: these are the manifold grace of God at work. Your gift is not a smaller version of someone else’s; it is the one God chose for you.
self_statements: What I do doesn’t really count.
God uses other people, not me.
I don’t have any real gifts.
Nobody would miss what I do.
If I were more gifted, I’d matter more.
errors: Measuring your gift against someone else’s instead of against God’s design.
Shrinking the value of quiet or hidden service.
Dismissing thanks or evidence that God has used you.
“I should have a more impressive gift.”
questions: Who decided where I fit in the body of Christ?
What does Paul say about the parts that seem weaker?
If the Spirit gives gifts to each one, what has He given me?
Has my quiet service ever made a difference in someone’s life?
Am I valuing gifts the way the world does, or the way God does?
Would the church be better off if everyone had the same gift?
Who in my church shows that hidden gifts matter?
truth: My spiritual gifts matter. God gave them to me on purpose, for the good of others. He arranged the body exactly as He wanted, and the parts that seem weaker are indispensable. I do not need to compare myself with anyone; I need to be a faithful steward of the grace God has given me.
hw_questions: Who decided where I fit in Christ’s body?
What does Paul say about the “weaker” parts?
What has the Spirit given me?
Has my quiet service made a difference?
Am I valuing gifts the way God does?
Would the church be better if everyone were the same?
hw_truths: God placed me in His body on purpose.
My gifts are given for the good of others.
The parts that seem weaker are indispensable.
I am a steward of God’s grace.
I do not need to compare my gift with anyone’s.
Small acts of service matter to God.
log: Each day, write one way God used me to help, encourage, or serve someone, no matter how small.
name_example: As a good steward of the manifold grace of God, Sarah should use whatever gift she has received to serve one another.
actions: “What do you think God has gifted me to do?” Write down every answer.
Use one gift on purpose this week,
such as encouraging, helping, giving, or praying, and notice the effect.
to someone whose hidden service you appreciate, and notice how much it matters.
and write which part of the body you are most like.
tracker: One way God used me today
prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for the gifts You have given me. Help me reject the lie that my gifts don’t matter as much as other people’s. Free me from comparison, and help me use what You have given me faithfully and joyfully to serve others. Thank You for placing me in Your body. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
